promptText: What project management tools exist for a startup founder working solo?
rawText:
As a solo startup founder, your biggest enemy isn’t competition—it’s **context switching** and **overhead**. You need a tool that helps you execute quickly without taking hours to maintain. 

The best tool depends on how your brain works and what kind of startup you are building. Here is a breakdown of the best project management tools for solo founders, categorized by their core strength.

---

### 1. The "All-in-One" Workspaces (Best for Centralizing Everything)
If you want your notes, task lists, roadmap, and company wiki all in one single app, choose one of these.

*   **Notion**
    *   **Best for:** Founders who want complete customization and a "second brain."
    *   **Why it works for solo founders:** You can build a custom CRM, content calendar, product roadmap, and investor list side-by-side with your daily tasks.
    *   **Downside:** Easy to spend days customizing templates instead of building your business.
    *   **Cost:** Generous Free tier.
*   **Coda**
    *   **Best for:** Founders who love spreadsheets, data automation, and dynamic documents.
    *   **Why it works:** It feels like a mix of Google Docs and Excel. It excels at auto-updating task lists and interactive widgets.
    *   **Cost:** Free tier available.

---

### 2. Developer & Product-Centric Tools (Best for Tech Founders)
If you are building software, managing git repositories, and tracking bug fixes or feature releases, general-purpose tools might feel too slow.

*   **Linear**
    *   **Best for:** Technical founders building software/SaaS products.
    *   **Why it works:** Blazing fast, keyboard-centric, and beautifully designed. It cuts out the clutter of Jira and connects seamlessly to GitHub/GitLab. You can map out high-level roadmaps down to specific lines of code.
    *   **Cost:** Free tier (up to 250 active issues).
*   **GitHub Projects**
    *   **Best for:** Solo devs who want zero context-switching outside their codebase.
    *   **Why it works:** Built right into GitHub. You convert code issues directly into Kanban cards. 
    *   **Cost:** Free.

---

### 3. Daily Focus & Time-Blocking Tools (Best for Managing Time & Burnout)
If your primary issue is deciding *what to do today* out of a massive, overwhelming backlog, these tools merge your task list directly with your Google/Outlook Calendar.

*   **Sunsama**
    *   **Best for:** Preventing burnout and forcing realistic daily workloads.
    *   **Why it works:** It pulls tasks from email, Notion, Trello, or GitHub, and forces you to drag them onto your calendar for a realistic daily schedule. It emphasizes ending your workday on time.
    *   **Cost:** Paid (~$16/mo, 14-day free trial).
*   **Motion**
    *   **Best for:** Automated scheduling.
    *   **Why it works:** Uses AI to automatically build your daily schedule around your meetings and task deadlines. If a task takes longer than expected, it reschedules the rest of your day automatically.
    *   **Cost:** Paid (Expensive at ~$19–$34/mo, but saves heavy planning time).
*   **Amplenote**
    *   **Best for:** The "Idea-to-Execution" pipeline.
    *   **Why it works:** Built on a four-step framework: Capture idea -> Convert to task -> Prioritize via Task Score -> Drag to calendar. 
    *   **Cost:** Generous Free tier.

---

### 4. Simple & Frictionless Kanban (Best for Speed)
If you just want a digital sticky-note board so you don't overthink things.

*   **Trello**
    *   **Best for:** Visual thinkers who want zero setup time.
    *   **Why it works:** Drag-and-drop cards across columns ("To Do", "In Progress", "Done"). It takes 30 seconds to set up.
    *   **Cost:** Free tier is usually all a solo founder needs.
*   **Todoist** or **TickTick**
    *   **Best for:** Fast task capture on mobile/desktop.
    *   **Why it works:** Quick natural language input (e.g., "Email pitch deck to John next Tuesday at 9am"). Great for catching random ideas while on the go.
    *   **Cost:** Free tiers available.

---

### Recommended Stacks for Solo Founders

Don't use five tools. Choose **one** of the following simple combinations:

1.  **The "Minimalist Tech Founder" Stack:**
    *   **Linear** (Product Roadmap & Dev tasks) + **Apple Notes / Obsidian** (Quick thoughts & docs).
2.  **The "All-in-One Operations" Stack:**
    *   **Notion** (Everything: Tasks, docs, CRM, roadmap).
3.  **The "Time-Constrained/Part-Time Founder" Stack:**
    *   **Sunsama or Motion** (Calendar & Task execution) + **Google Docs** (Product strategy/writing).

### The Golden Rule for Solo Founders
**Avoid "Tool-Admin" Trap.** If you spend more than 15 minutes a day *organizing* your project management tool, the tool is failing you. Pick the system with the lowest barrier to entry so you can spend 95% of your energy building and talking to customers.
